levels.title: A1 – Principiante
levels.description: First steps: introduce yourself, order, ask the way, talk about your day and what you like.

levels.title: A2 – Elementare
levels.description: Talk about the past, use pronouns and prepositions, make plans and compare. Open any time as a refresher.

levels.title: B1 – Intermedio
levels.description: Narrate past events, handle everyday services, give opinions and make plans with confidence.

levels.title: B2 – Intermedio superiore
levels.description: Argue, hypothesise and report in detail; understand news, notices and longer conversations.

levels.title: C1 – Avanzato
levels.description: Use Italian flexibly and precisely across registers: formal writing, nuance, idiom and mediation.

levels.title: Esame CELI 3 (B2)
levels.description: Exam preparation for CELI 3: every section of the exam, strategies and timed mock papers.

units.title: Ciao, sono…
units.summary: Greetings, essere and the alphabet to introduce yourself and spell your name.

units.title: Un caffè e due cornetti
units.summary: Noun gender and number with definite and indefinite articles.

units.title: Che cosa fai?
units.summary: Regular -are verbs in the present to talk about work, study and everyday actions.

units.title: La mia giornata
units.summary: Regular -ere and -ire verbs (including -isc-) and telling the time to describe your day.

units.title: Al bar e al mercato
units.summary: Numbers, prices, vorrei and quanto costa to order and shop.

units.title: Dov'è la stazione?
units.summary: C'è / ci sono, simple prepositions and directions to find places in town.

units.title: Vado, faccio, vengo
units.summary: The key irregular verbs: andare, fare, venire, avere, volere, potere, dovere, uscire.

units.title: Mi piace!
units.summary: Piacere, adverbs of frequency and free time.

units.title: La mia famiglia
units.summary: Possessive adjectives with family words, and describing people.

units.title: Ripasso A1
units.summary: A1 checkpoint: introduce yourself, order, ask the way and talk about your week.

units.title: Il passato prossimo
units.summary: Passato prossimo with avere or essere, irregular participles and agreement, to say what you did yesterday or last weekend.

units.title: L'imperfetto
units.summary: Imperfetto forms and core uses (habits, descriptions, background) to describe how things used to be.

units.title: Che cosa stai facendo?
units.summary: Stare + gerundio and stare per to say what is happening now or about to happen.

units.title: Preposizioni articolate
units.summary: Articles and articulated prepositions (al, nel, dal, sul…) to say where things are and how to get somewhere.

units.title: Pronomi diretti e indiretti
units.summary: Direct and indirect object pronouns (lo, la, gli, le…) to handle everyday shopping and service exchanges.

units.title: La giornata e i riflessivi
units.summary: Reflexive verbs in the present and passato prossimo to describe daily routines.

units.title: Futuro e confronti
units.summary: Futuro semplice plus comparatives and superlatives to talk about plans and compare options.

units.title: Mi piacerebbe…
units.summary: Piacere in the past and mi piacerebbe / vorrei to talk about tastes and wishes.

units.title: Fai così!
units.summary: The informal imperative (tu, voi, noi) with and without pronouns to give friendly instructions.

units.title: Ripasso A2
units.summary: A2 checkpoint: talk about the past, plans and preferences in everyday situations.

units.title: Com'è andata?
units.summary: Passato prossimo vs imperfetto to tell someone how a recent day, appointment or weekend went.

units.title: Ci e ne
units.summary: The particles ci and ne to talk about places and quantities at the market, shops and home.

units.title: Me lo dà?
units.summary: Combined pronouns (me lo, glielo, ce ne…) to ask for, offer and return things at the pharmacy, post office or shop.

units.title: Ripasso 1
units.summary: Checkpoint reviewing past tenses, ci/ne and combined pronouns through a mixed real-life task set.

units.title: Come si fa?
units.summary: Si impersonale and the imperative (tu and Lei, with pronouns) to understand and give instructions and procedures.

units.title: Vorrei sapere…
units.summary: Condizionale presente to make polite requests, give advice and express wishes on the phone and at the counter.

units.title: Progetti e previsioni
units.summary: Futuro semplice and futuro anteriore to make plans, set deadlines and guess about the present and past.

units.title: Ripasso 2
units.summary: Checkpoint reviewing instructions, conditional and future through an appointment-booking and planning task.

units.title: Che cos'è il congiuntivo?
units.summary: Recognise the congiuntivo and build the regular presente in three small steps: -are, then -ere and -ire, then -isc- verbs.

units.title: Irregolari senza paura
units.summary: Sixteen key irregular congiuntivo forms in four families of four, built from the io form of the present (faccio → faccia).

units.title: Penso, spero, ho paura
units.summary: The five trigger families (opinion, will, emotion, doubt, impersonal), versus the indicative after certainty and di + infinitive with the same subject.

units.title: Penso che sia già partito
units.summary: Congiuntivo passato for earlier actions seen from now: credo che sia vs credo che sia stato, plus a checkpoint on CG1–CG4.

units.title: La persona che cerco
units.summary: Relative pronouns (che, cui, chi, quello che) to describe people, things and what you need.

units.title: Era già successo
units.summary: Trapassato prossimo and time connectors (prima, dopo, appena, ormai) to tell a story in a clear sequence.

units.title: Ripasso B1
units.summary: End-of-B1 checkpoint: narrating, opining and handling services across all B1 grammar.

units.title: Benché, purché, prima che
units.summary: Conjunctions that always take the congiuntivo, perché for purpose vs cause, and prima che / senza che vs prima di / senza + infinitive.

units.title: Pensavo che fosse
units.summary: Congiuntivo imperfetto and trapassato, and the concordanza dei tempi in one picture: penso che venga / pensavo che venisse.

units.title: Se fosse possibile…
units.summary: Periodo ipotetico types 1 and 2 to discuss real and hypothetical options and their consequences.

units.title: Avrei voluto…
units.summary: Condizionale passato to express regrets, the future in the past and unconfirmed news.

units.title: Ripasso 3
units.summary: Checkpoint reviewing subjunctive, conditional and hypotheticals through a complaint-and-negotiation task.

units.title: Si comunica che…
units.summary: The passive (essere, venire, andare + participle, si passivante) to understand and write news, notices and official announcements.

units.title: Mi ha detto che…
units.summary: Reported speech with tense shifts to pass on what a doctor, teacher or official said.

units.title: Ripasso 4
units.summary: Checkpoint reviewing passive, reported speech and sequence of tenses through a news-and-retell task.

units.title: Se l'avessi saputo…
units.summary: Hypotheticals with the congiuntivo: se fosse… sarebbe, se avessi saputo… avrei, mixed conditionals, magari and come se.

units.title: Detto fatto
units.summary: Gerundio, participio and infinito in implicit clauses to make sentences shorter and more fluent.

units.title: Ripasso B2
units.summary: End-of-B2 checkpoint: argue, report and hypothesise in extended speech and writing.

units.title: Registro e cortesia
units.summary: Formal register and nominalisation to write effective formal emails, complaints and requests.

units.title: Il passato remoto
units.summary: Passato remoto (recognition and active use) to read and retell narratives, history and literary texts.

units.title: È lui che…
units.summary: Marked word order (dislocation, cleft sentences) to sound natural and emphasise ideas in speech.

units.title: Ripasso 5
units.summary: Checkpoint reviewing register, passato remoto and marked word order through a formal-and-informal retelling task.

units.title: Modi di dire
units.summary: Idioms and strong collocations to understand and use colloquial, vivid Italian appropriately.

units.title: Cavarsela
units.summary: Pronominal verbs (farcela, cavarsela, prendersela, andarsene) to talk about coping, conflict and emotions.

units.title: Il burocratese
units.summary: Bureaucratic language and impersonal constructions to read contracts, forms and official letters.

units.title: Chiunque sia
units.summary: The congiuntivo for nuance: relatives (il primo che, l'unico che), indefinites (chiunque, qualunque), superlatives, independent uses, and when spoken Italian drops it.

units.title: Discutere e mediare
units.summary: Discourse markers, hedging and mitigation to lead discussions, disagree politely and mediate.

units.title: Ripasso finale
units.summary: Final C1 checkpoint: extended argument, mediation and formal writing across the whole course.

units.title: Leggere per l'esame
units.summary: Reading (Part A): multiple choice on two texts, comparing two texts and open questions, with paraphrase strategies.

units.title: Ascoltare per l'esame
units.summary: Listening (Part D, 25 min): multiple choice on news, announcements, interviews and phone-ins, and completing sentences with words from the recording.

units.title: Competenza linguistica
units.summary: Language competence (Part C, 45 min): two cloze texts, rebuilding sentences with connectives, and word formation.

units.title: Scrivere per l'esame
units.summary: Writing (Part B): an 80–100-word letter or email and a 120–180-word composition, self-checked against the official criteria.

units.title: Parlare per l'esame
units.summary: Speaking (about 15 min plus 15 min prep): self-presentation, describing a photo, summarising a short text and a role-play.

units.title: Simulazione d'esame
units.summary: Timed mock of all three booklets and the oral, with self-assessment against the official criteria and pass marks.
